title: The Leiden Manifesto for research metrics
abstract: Data are increasingly used to govern science. Research evaluations that were once bespoke and conducted by peers are now routinely aided by metrics. The problem is that evaluation is now led by the data rather than by judgment. Metrics have proliferated: usually well intentioned, not always well informed, often ill applied. We present ten principles to guide research evaluation, emphasizing that quantitative evaluation should support qualitative, expert assessment and protect local research excellence.

title: San Francisco Declaration on Research Assessment: Putting science into the assessment of research
abstract: The San Francisco Declaration on Research Assessment (DORA) recognizes the need to improve the ways in which the outputs of scholarly research are evaluated. It recommends eliminating the use of journal-based metrics, such as Journal Impact Factors, in funding, appointment, and promotion decisions, assessing research on its own merits rather than on the basis of the journal in which it is published, and capitalizing on the opportunities provided by online publication.

title: A review of the use and misuse of citation indicators in research evaluation
abstract: Citation indicators are widely used in research evaluation, but their appropriate use requires a deep understanding of their properties and limitations. This paper provides a comprehensive review of citation indicators, covering direct citation counts, h-index, field normalization, and fractional counting. We analyze common pitfalls, including unadjusted cross-disciplinary comparisons, metric gaming, and the neglect of qualitative peer review in assessing individual researchers.

title: The Hong Kong Principles for assessing researchers: Fostering research integrity
abstract: Research assessment criteria often reward quantity over quality and rigor, which may inadvertently incentivize poor research practices. The Hong Kong Principles provide a framework to reward responsible research practices, open science, replication studies, transparent reporting, and peer review contributions to foster a research culture based on integrity.

title: Assessing research impact: Moving beyond citations and the h-index
abstract: Bibliometric indicators such as citation counts and the h-index have become standard tools for evaluating researchers. However, reliance on single metrics introduces severe biases against early-career researchers, interdisciplinary scholarship, and non-traditional scholarly outputs. We argue for a multidimensional, contextualized evaluation portfolio integrating qualitative peer evidence.

title: OpenAlex: A fully-open index of scholarly works, authors, institutions, and concepts
abstract: OpenAlex is a free, openly accessible scholarly graph containing hundreds of millions of interconnected research entities including scientific works, authors, institutions, and topics. Designed as an open replacement for proprietary bibliographic databases like Web of Science and Scopus, OpenAlex empowers researchers to audit citations and build transparent, reproducible research evaluation tools.

title: Field-normalized citation indicators: Normalization methods and validation across disciplines
abstract: Comparing raw citation numbers across different scientific disciplines produces misleading results because citation frequencies vary by orders of magnitude between fields. This study presents and validates advanced field-normalization approaches, including source-normalized and target-normalized indicators, providing standards for fair institutional comparison.
venue: Journal of the American Society for Information Science and Technology

title: Citation gaming, cartels, and strategic manipulation of bibliometric indicators
abstract: When indicators become targets for evaluation, they cease to be good metrics. This paper investigates gaming behavior in academic publishing, including coercive citations, citation cartels, and deliberate metric manipulation. We demonstrate how multi-level auditing frameworks can detect anomalous citation clustering and protect research integrity.

title: Altmetrics: Value, diversity, and limitations of alternative web-based metrics
abstract: Altmetrics track the attention research receives online, including downloads, social media mentions, blog posts, and policy document citations. While altmetrics provide rapid feedback and capture non-academic societal impact, they must not replace peer review or traditional indicators. We discuss their responsible combination in research evaluation.

title: KeyBERT: Minimal keyword extraction with contextual pre-trained language models
abstract: KeyBERT is a minimal and easy-to-use keyword extraction technique that leverages BERT-style contextual embeddings to create keywords and keyphrases that are most similar to a document. By computing cosine similarity between candidate sub-phrases and the global document representation, KeyBERT achieves state-of-the-art keyphrase relevance without manual supervision.

title: Sentence-BERT: Sentence embeddings using Siamese BERT-networks
abstract: BERT and RoBERTa have set new state-of-the-art performance on sentence-pair regression tasks like semantic textual similarity. However, comparing two sentences requires feeding both into the network, causing massive computational overhead. We present Sentence-BERT (SBERT), a modification of the pre-trained BERT network that uses siamese and triplet network structures to derive semantically meaningful sentence embeddings that can be compared using cosine similarity.

title: SciBERT: A pretrained language model for scientific text
abstract: Obtaining pre-trained models on scientific text is essential for scientific NLP tasks such as information extraction, citation intent classification, and research gap detection. SciBERT is a pre-trained language model based on BERT trained on a large corpus of scientific publications from biomedical and computer science domains, showing substantial improvements over standard BERT on scientific benchmarks.

title: Federated Learning: Challenges, methods, and future directions
abstract: Federated learning involves training statistical models over decentralized devices holding local data samples without exchanging them. This survey discusses privacy guarantees, communication-efficient distributed optimization, system and statistical heterogeneity across clients, and multi-modal decoupled federated learning architectures.

title: Communication-efficient learning of deep networks from decentralized data
abstract: Modern mobile devices have access to a wealth of data suitable for learning models. However, this data is often privacy-sensitive. We introduce FederatedAveraging (FedAvg), an algorithm that decouples model training from direct raw data access by aggregating locally computed gradient updates on central servers.

title: Modality-decoupled and heterogeneous representations in distributed collaborative learning
abstract: Real-world collaborative learning systems often suffer from severe modality discrepancies and client-level data heterogeneity. This paper investigates modality-decoupled collaborative frameworks that enable clients with missing or heterogeneous sensory modalities to exchange representations efficiently without degrading global convergence.
venue: IEEE Transactions on Neural Networks and Learning Systems

title: Visuotactile world models for robotic manipulation and state estimation
abstract: Robust physical interaction in robotics requires understanding both visual scenes and tactile contact feedback. We propose a compact visuotactile predictive world model that learns unified latent representations from multi-modal sensor streams to predict contact dynamics and plan robotic manipulation tasks under occlusion.

title: The INORMS SCOPE framework for responsible research evaluation
abstract: The International Network of Research Management Societies (INORMS) developed the SCOPE framework to guide universities and funding agencies in evaluating research responsibly: Start with values, Context consideration, Options exploration, Probe deeply, and Evaluate effectiveness.

title: Responsible metrics in institutional rankings: Towards fair university comparisons
abstract: Commercial global university rankings frequently violate responsible metrics principles by assigning arbitrary weights to composite indicators. This paper proposes a transparent, field-normalized benchmarking framework that discourages ranking gaming and emphasizes social impact and educational quality.

title: Automated detection of research problem statements and methodology in scientific literature
abstract: Understanding the structure of scholarly discourse is fundamental for automated literature synthesis. We develop an NLP pipeline using sequence labeling and sentence transformers to extract explicit research problem statements, methodology descriptions, and key findings from scientific PDF papers.

title: Research gap detection using semantic networks and literature embedding graphs
abstract: Identifying unexplored research gaps is critical for scientific breakthrough. We construct literature embedding graphs and compute concept density across thematic clusters, pinpointing underexplored scientific keywords and bridging disparate disciplinary silos.
